summary: The RUN-LEVEL recommendation-skip record (cinatra#2794 S9b) — the operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap leaf runRecommendationSkipsSchemaQueries in src/lib/artifacts/artifact-review-gate-schema.ts, spread into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries in the SAME PR. ONE brand-new table, run_recommendation_skips, that gives a skipped run's decision a record keyed by the RUN rather than by a skill. THE DEFECT: a skip is a decision about the run and the run-start recommendation card settles only when that decision is on record, but the record lived in run_rejected_recommendations, which is keyed (run_id, skill_id) — so a skip that named no skill (drift retired every offered candidate while the run sat parked, or the template read back with no package name) had no row to occupy; the stop-gap was a RESERVED skill id, __run_level_skip__, written into that table as though it were a skill. WHY THE STOP-GAP COULD NOT STAY: skill ids are caller-provided text (createOrUpdateSkill takes input.skillId verbatim in packages/skills/src/skills-store.ts) and no constraint excludes the reserved value, so a real skill can carry that id, and one collision produces two failures — the efficacy reader filtered the id out, silently dropping a genuine rejected skill from the accepted/rejected split, and a genuine rejection could be misread as a run-level marker. SHAPE: one row per run — run_id is the PRIMARY KEY, so the write is naturally idempotent and a retried skip (a lost response, a double-click) converges on the same row instead of duplicating; skipped_by names the principal whose decision it was (the skip path is fail-closed on run.runBy === userId, so it is always known at write time); candidate_count carries the fact the sentinel row destroyed — how many per-skill efficacy rows accompanied this skip, 0 meaning the scorer returned nothing to name — so the efficacy split can tell those apart without inventing a rejected skill; skipped_at is the decision's own clock. NO FOREIGN KEY, deliberately, on the sibling precedent: both members of this family — run_selected_skill_revisions (core__0079) and run_rejected_recommendations (core__0081) — carry a bare run_id text NOT NULL and are read beside this record by the same efficacy path; behaviourally, a failed marker write now refuses the skip and leaves the park live, so an FK would turn a benign race (the run row deleted concurrently) into a user-visible refusal on a decision that is otherwise fine. ADDITIVE (one brand-new empty table plus one index) — no artifact is required by the convention, shipped anyway on the core__0067 / 0072 / 0093 precedent so fresh-install and operator-upgrade paths stay aligned: an already-running instance never re-runs the bootstrap DDL, so without this module the table would exist on fresh installs only and on an upgraded instance every skip would fail its marker write and refuse, leaving the hold undecidable. The DDL mirrors the bootstrap leaf exactly (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS): a no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install, executed by db migrate on an existing deployment; unqualified names ride the runner's search_path (the app schema); metadata-only DDL on an empty table, no noTransaction(). NO BACKFILL, deliberately: runs skipped before this migration carry their evidence as user_skipped rows in run_rejected_recommendations and hasRunRecommendationSkip reads the run-level record OR that legacy evidence, so an already-skipped run's card keeps settling; backfilling would have to invent a skipped_by the old rows never recorded. down() drops the table IF EXISTS (reversible; the index rides the table drop; HONEST COST: run-level skip markers are lost, so a skip that named no candidate loses its only evidence and its card reverts to unsettled, which an operator-initiated --down accepts). SEQ 0094 — strictly greater than the max shipped seq on origin/main (core__0093 agent-run-hitl-gate-artifacts). SEQ IS PROVISIONAL: a concurrent lane may claim 0094 first, in which case a rename-only renumber is normal (FLAGGED for the coordinator's train). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
